note: These sources motivate the evaluation design. They are not findings from this cohort.

sources.citation: Lewis, P., Perez, E., Piktus, A., Petroni, F., Karpukhin, V., Goyal, N., Küttler, H., Lewis, M., Yih, W., Rocktäschel, T., Riedel, S., & Kiela, D. (2020). Retrieval-augmented generation for knowledge-intensive NLP tasks. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 33.
sources.recommendation: RAG combines a retriever over an external corpus with a generator conditioned on the retrieved passages.
sources.use_in_this_project: The definition was used to classify the pipeline. Rubrics are pasted into prompts and pages are supplied directly, so retrieval metrics were not calculated.
sources.not_implemented: No dense index, no ranked passages, and no citation-grounded generation.

sources.citation: Gao, Y., Xiong, Y., Gao, X., Jia, K., Pan, J., Bi, Y., Dai, Y., Sun, J., Wang, M., & Wang, H. (2023). Retrieval-augmented generation for large language models: A survey. arXiv:2312.10997.
sources.recommendation: Evaluate retrieval and generation separately, then the combined system.
sources.use_in_this_project: The separation was kept. Because retrieval is absent, only the generation-side tasks that actually exist were examined: extraction, rubric scoring, and frame coding.
sources.not_implemented: The survey's retrieval benchmarks do not apply.

sources.citation: Es, S., James, J., Espinosa Anke, L., & Schockaert, S. (2024). RAGAs: Automated evaluation of retrieval augmented generation. Proceedings of the 18th Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: System Demonstrations, 150–158.
sources.recommendation: Faithfulness, answer relevance, and context relevance are different qualities. An automatic judge is not itself the reference.
sources.use_in_this_project: No RAGAs score was produced. The paper is cited to explain why an LLM judge was not treated as ground truth for rubric scores or frame labels.
sources.not_implemented: No human-compared sample of faithfulness judgements.

sources.citation: Saad-Falcon, J., Khattab, O., Potts, C., & Zaharia, M. (2024). ARES: An automated evaluation framework for retrieval-augmented generation systems. Proceedings of the 2024 Conference of the North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies, 338–354.
sources.recommendation: Automated RAG judges still need a human annotation set if their error is to be bounded.
sources.use_in_this_project: Used as a reason not to invent a RAG score. The human work still required here is a second coding of frames and an independent rescore of rubric items.

sources.citation: Di Mitri, D., Schneider, J., Specht, M., & Drachsler, H. (2018). From signals to knowledge: A conceptual model for multimodal learning analytics. Journal of Computer Assisted Learning, 34(4), 338–349.
sources.recommendation: Sensors record observable events. Cognitions and intentions are latent and need a separate interpretive step.
sources.use_in_this_project: Log rows and frame labels are reported as observable records. Threshold-then-different-accuracy is reported as a temporal association, not as an intention.
sources.not_implemented: No validated indicator of confusion, confidence, or strategy was added.

sources.citation: Sharma, K., & Giannakos, M. (2020). Multimodal data capabilities for learning: What can multimodal data tell us about learning? British Journal of Educational Technology, 51(5), 1450–1484.
sources.recommendation: Multimodal claims should state the learning question, the modalities, and what each modality can and cannot show.
sources.use_in_this_project: Worksheets, frames, logs, and final files were described separately before the session-level comparison. Co-occurrence was classified as complementary rather than as confirmation of the same event.
sources.not_implemented: No cross-modal fusion model was trained.

sources.citation: Ferguson, R., & Clow, D. (2017). Where is the evidence? A call to action for learning analytics. Proceedings of the Seventh International Learning Analytics & Knowledge Conference, 56–65.
sources.recommendation: Do not treat a logged activity or a research pipeline as evidence that learning improved.
sources.use_in_this_project: The evaluation stops at record quality, score-file consistency, and coverage. It does not estimate a learning gain.
sources.not_implemented: No outcome measure of teaching or learning improvement.

sources.citation: Cohen, J. (1960). A coefficient of agreement for nominal scales. Educational and Psychological Measurement, 20(1), 37–46.
sources.recommendation: For two coders and nominal labels, report raw agreement and a chance-corrected coefficient.
sources.use_in_this_project: Named as the appropriate future statistic for a second coding of the behaviour labels.
sources.not_implemented: No second coder, so kappa was not calculated.
